summary: Service identity bridge role evaluated as DENY for cross-account KMS writes from analytics cluster
description: Issue summary: Analytics ETL jobs running in the analytics cluster fail intermittently when attempting to encrypt artifacts to cross-account S3 buckets that require AWS KMS CMK encryption. Background: We use a service-identity bridge (GCP -> AWS) to allow the analytics GKE workloads to assume a short-lived AWS role which in turn is allowed to use a customer-managed KMS key. Starting 2026-03-09 we began seeing DENY results in the IAM policy evaluation for kms:Encrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey when the bridged role performs writes. Impact: P1 internal outage for analytics pipelines; nightly ETL failing ~35% of runs, downstream data availability and billing reconciliation pipelines delayed. Workaround: Re-running jobs under a fallback local CMK (non-cross-account) succeeds but violates data partitioning SLA. Environment: prod:us-west cluster (gke-analytics-prod), bridged AWS account: rw-infra-analytics (acct 123456789012), CMK alias: alias/analytics-crossaccount-cmk. Steps to reproduce: 1) Trigger nightly ETL job that writes encrypted artifact to s3://rw-analytics-shared 2) Observe job fail during KMSEncrypt step 3) Check AWS CloudTrail and Policy Simulator for the short-lived role credentials Observed behavior: IAM policy evaluator returns explicit DENY for kms:Encrypt calls from AssumeRole session with arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/bridge-analytics-role/session-*. Expected behavior: Role should be permitted to use the CMK for Encrypt/GenerateDataKey as per cross-account key policy and IAM role inline allow. Note: Key policy was last modified 2026-02-22 and role trust policy unchanged. We suspect a policy condition related to aws:SourceAccount or encryption-context mismatch being evaluated during STS session. Next steps are listed in investigation_notes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On GKE analytics-prod, run the ETL job 'etl-artifact-upload' which calls kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Encrypt via the bridged AWS role. 2) Observe task fail with Code 400/AccessDenied at kms.Encrypt. 3) Collect GCP audit log for the workload identity token exchange and AWS CloudTrail entries for AssumeRole + KMS calls.
logs: CloudTrail snippet: 2026-03-10T03:12:21Z AssumeRoleAction: Success, principal: arn:iam::PROJECT:role/bridge-analytics-role; 2026-03-10T03:12:22Z KMS Encrypt: ResponseElements: null; ErrorCode: AccessDeniedException; ErrorMessage: User is not authorized to perform kms:Encrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345. GCP workload identity audit: token exchange ID tok-9a8b7c, audience=arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/bridge-analytics-role. Policy simulator output attached in S3.
investigation_notes: Initial checks: 1) Verified role mapping in bridge service returned correct session name and tags. 2) Confirmed IAM role has inline policy allowing kms:Encrypt on the CMK. 3) Key policy contains Allow for the role principal but contains a Condition restricting usage to aws:SourceAccount == 987654321098 (legacy analytics account), which does not match current bridged account 123456789012. Hypothesis: Key policy condition mismatch causes explicit DENY in evaluator. Secondary hypothesis: Session tags used by bridge are not propagated to KMS context, causing condition on encryption context to fail. Actions taken: - Pulled key policy and compared against PR #2387 which updated cross-account bindings in Feb; noticed early condition left referencing legacy account. - Ran aws kms simulate-principal-policy with session ARN and got explicit DENY indicating key policy condition failure. - Scoped test: temporarily updated key policy to allow account 123456789012 (safe test) and ETL succeeded for 3 runs. This suggests key policy is the root cause. Constraints: Need stakeholder approval before making key policy change permanent; encryption governance owner is Security/KeyOps.

Follow-ups: 1) Security to approve CR-2026-183 and schedule key policy change in maintenance window. 2) Update Confluence runbook to document cross-account CMK ownership and lifecycle. 3) Add an alert that checks for mismatched key policy SourceAccount entries when onboarding new bridged accounts. 4) Consider updating bridge to tag sessions with encryption-context that matches key policy conditions.
